question: Why do openalex_semantic and openalex_combined_semantic report Hit@20 identical to Hit@50 while returning a mean of 45.92 results?
what_relevance_score_is: OpenAlex's own relevance_score field, selected in the request and stored verbatim by scripts/openalex-records.mjs (w.relevance_score ?? null). Hits are stored in the order the API returned them; nothing in our pipeline re-sorts them. For search.semantic the values sit in a narrow band just below and above 1.0, consistent with an embedding similarity; for keyword search they are BM25-scale, in the hundreds.

H1_score_collapses_at_rank_20.evidence: relevance_score is monotonically non-increasing across all 50 ranks in every OpenAlex arm, with zero monotonicity breaks. There is no discontinuity at 20. What the semantic arms do show is saturation: mean score falls 1.1529 -> 0.9164 over ranks 1-20 and only 0.9164 -> 0.8936 over ranks 20-50, a 2.22% relative decline across the tail against 27.1% for the keyword control. Consecutive-rank gaps flatten by 17.78x. So the tail is weakly ordered, not unordered, and saturation alone does not produce a hard zero.

H2_null_or_zero_scores_past_20.evidence: Zero null and zero zero-valued relevance_score values in any band of any OpenAlex arm: 3949 scored slots for openalex_semantic, all populated.

H3_tail_is_recycled_or_off_population.evidence: No document repeats inside any list and no pair of questions shares a single tail document, so nothing is being recycled or dumped. The composition, however, changes sharply with depth. For openalex_semantic, mean citations fall 155.51 (ranks 1-10) -> 1.24 (ranks 21-50), median 0, with 75.91% of tail documents uncited; 85.24% carry no PMID and 35.35% carry neither DOI nor PMID. The keyword control over the same depth stays inside the indexed journal literature: 265.92 mean citations, 15.13% without a PMID, 1.79% unmatchable.

H4_our_per_page_handling.evidence: The request is a single page, per-page=<depth>, with no cursor and no second call, so there is nothing to re-order. Lists are not capped at 20: 86/86 openalex_semantic lists exceed 20 results and every list reaches rank 25. The shortfall behind the 45.92 mean begins in the far tail, not at 20, so it cannot manufacture a rank-20 boundary. Live control: per-page=50 returns the same first twenty, in the same order, with the same scores, as per-page=20. Our request shape does not create the boundary.

H5_targets_present_but_unmatchable.supported: no — the identifier rule is conservative but it did not hide a tail recovery
H5_targets_present_but_unmatchable.evidence: No recorded miss contains its target by DOI or by PMID, so the scorer is faithful to its own rule. A normalised-title sweep over all 50 ranks flagged 2 of 60 misses, of which 3 sit past rank 20. Inspecting them settles the question: not one is the target's own record — every flagged hit is a separate OpenAlex work with a different DOI. The tail case is a zero-citation duplicate of a 1,866-citation article, carrying a minted non-publisher DOI and appearing three times in the same list under three different identifiers, which is an instance of the mechanism rather than a scoring failure. The head case is a same-title journal record with a different DOI and PMID at rank 1, which does not bear on the tail at all. The ceiling is nonetheless real in principle: 35.35% of semantic tail slots carry neither identifier, so identifier matching is structurally blind to about a third of the tail, and the surprise calculation is reported both with and without that discount.

plateau_surprise.caveat: The reference ratio is an empirical extrapolation from six other arms, not a model of OpenAlex. It sets the order of magnitude of the surprise, not a precise p.

is_rank_20_a_real_boundary.answer: no — there is no discontinuity at 20 in any measurable quantity
is_rank_20_a_real_boundary.evidence: The deepest successful find is rank 20 for openalex_semantic and rank 19 for openalex_combined_semantic, so the two arms do not in fact stop at the same rank. Because the run reports Hit@1, @10, @20 and @50 and nothing between, both appear to plateau "at exactly 20". The score curve is smooth and monotone through the boundary and the composition gradient is smooth as well. What is real is a saturation region that has set in by roughly rank 20; where precisely it sets in is not resolvable from 25 and 31 finds.

live_control.verdict: per-page=50 returns the same first twenty, in the same order, with the same scores, as per-page=20. Our request shape does not create the boundary.

conclusion: The plateau is OpenAlex's behaviour, not our artefact — but it is not a boundary at rank 20, and the paper should not describe it as one. Four candidate mechanisms are rejected on the captured data. The relevance_score does not collapse, flatten to a constant, go null, or lose its ordering: every OpenAlex arm is monotonically non-increasing across all fifty ranks with zero breaks, and all 3949 scored slots per semantic arm carry a real non-zero value. No document repeats inside a list and no two questions share a single tail document, so nothing is recycled or dumped. The request is a single un-paginated page; all 86 semantic lists exceed 20 results and the count shortfall behind the 45.92 mean begins at rank 26, in the far tail, so it cannot manufacture a boundary at 20. And no recorded miss hides its target: a normalised-title sweep flagged two lists per semantic arm, and on inspection every flagged hit is a different OpenAlex work with a different DOI, not the target record. The mechanism the data does support is compositional. OpenAlex semantic search leaves the indexed journal literature as depth increases, and it does so far faster than OpenAlex keyword search on the same request. Over ranks 1-10, 11-20 and 21-50, mean citations of the returned documents fall 155.51 -> 12.25 -> 1.24 (tail median 0, 75.91% uncited), while the share carrying no PMID rises 21.86% -> 52.91% -> 85.24% and the share carrying neither DOI nor PMID rises 5% -> 19.53% -> 35.35%. openalex_keyword, requested at the same depth and returning a comparable 45.41 results, shows almost none of this: 265.92 mean citations, 15.13% without a PMID and 1.79% without either identifier at ranks 21-50. The semantic tail is thus populated by a different class of record — largely uncited, largely absent from PubMed, often without a DOI, and sometimes a duplicate stub of an article whose real record the same search failed to return. A PubMed-indexed target article is not a member of that population, which is why the tail never yields one. This is coherent with the score saturating: past rank 20 the semantic score spans only 2.22% of its value against 27.1% for keyword, a 17.78x flattening of the consecutive-rank gap, so the model has effectively stopped discriminating and the remaining slots are filled by whatever the embedding neighbourhood contains. Two honest limits. First, rank 20 is not special. The deepest find is rank 20 in one semantic arm and rank 19 in the other, so they do not stop at the same rank; the apparent coincidence comes from reporting Hit@1/@10/@20/@50 and nothing between. Nothing measurable is discontinuous at 20. What exists is a saturation region that has set in by roughly rank 20, and its exact onset is not resolvable from 25 and 31 successful placements. Second, the zero itself is only moderately surprising. Calibrating against the six other arms, openalex_semantic was due about 4.12 finds in ranks 21-50 (Poisson p of seeing none 0.0163, or 0.0698 once discounted for the third of tail slots identifier matching cannot see) and openalex_combined_semantic about 3.29 (p 0.0371 -> 0.1172). Neither arm is individually decisive. What makes the account credible is the two arms agreeing plus a measured compositional gradient that predicts the outcome and that the keyword control does not share. The claim to publish is "OpenAlex semantic retrieval degrades into uncited, non-PubMed-indexed and partly identifier-less records within the first few tens of ranks", not "it stops ranking at 20".
